findings.title: Materials' 52-point lens gap
findings.body: Materials trades at 16.91x forward but 35.32x trailing, a 52-point percentile gap between the two lenses. That gap implies analysts expect 109 percent earnings growth next year, a bet that current depressed earnings are a trough, not a new normal.

findings.title: Health Care's extreme forward percentile
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E sits at the 99th percentile of its five-year range, yet the multiple compressed 45 percent from trailing earnings. The market is underwriting an 81 percent earnings surge, a level of optimism that leaves no room for disappointment.

findings.title: Utilities' trailing percentile collapse
findings.body: Utilities' trailing P/E is at the 2nd percentile of its five-year range while its forward P/E is at the 28th, a 26-point gap. With only 4 percent implied earnings growth, the forward lens is not rescuing the sector—it is merely reflecting that reported earnings have already cratered.
